newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel favours easing resident forex controls.
newsitem.headline: India panel favours easing resident forex controls.

text.p: A panel set up by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Tuesday it favoured allowing resident Indians to invest in foreign currency denominated deposits with banks and individual companies in the country.
The panel, charged with plotting the path toward freeing the exchange rate, recommended the rupee be prepared for full covertibility in the next three years.
The foreign currency deposits would be permitted without a ceiling and the settlement would be in rupees, it said.

It recommended that individuals be allowed to invest in assets in global financial markets up to an amount of $25,000 in phase one with a progressive increase to $50,000 in phase two and $100,000 in phase three of phased covertibility of the Indian rupee.
Investments in global markets by residents are currently not permitted.

The panel said it favoured allowing residents to obtain loans from non-residents up to $250,000 per individual in phase one of convertibility with the payment of interest not exceeding LIBOR, without restrictions on the period of the loan, the repatriation of principal/interest and the use of funds.
The loan amount should be increased to $500,000 in phase two and to $1.0 million in the third phase of capital convertibility, the panel recommended.
Currently, RBI allows interest free loans on a non-repatriation basis from non-resident relatives for personal and business purposes other than investment.

The panel said it favoured capital transfers from non repatriable assets held in India by non-resident Indians for an amount up to $25,000 per year in phase one, $50,000 per year in phase two and $100,000 in phase three.
Non-resident Indians would not need RBI permission for foreign direct investment in India (other than in real estate) subject to reporting by authorised foreign exchange dealers, the panel said.
Currently foreign direct investment with repatriation benefits are cleared by the RBI and the government.
